items.doc: David N. Baker SI-NEA oral history (2)
items.title: David N. Baker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: my cousin Walter, who was at that time welterweight champ of the state, or runner-up. He played bebop.

ctx.x: On the streetcar. They put me off there several times. I remember one girl who was kind of a tough girl who went to high school, and she told me she would kick my butt if I brought that tuba and played it on there again. I believed it, so I didn’t do that any more. [laughter] But I had that E-flat tuba. It’s a wonder there was any connubial bliss, because my stepmother would go to her sister's, who lived – let me see see: [Baker names the streets] Columbia, Martindale, Arsenal, and Sheldon – lived blocks away.
